"'''Picture'''" is a [[duet]] written by American music artists [[Kid Rock]] and [[Sheryl Crow]], released on November 12, 2002, as the fourth single and ninth track from Kid Rock's 2001 album ''[[Cocky (album)|Cocky]]''. The original recording on the album is performed by the song's writers. Rock re-recorded the song for radio with [[alternative country]] singer [[Allison Moorer]] because Atlantic was initially unable to get the rights from Crow's label to release the album version as a single.<ref name=Kaufman/> When the Moorer version was released, some radio stations began playing the Crow version instead, leading ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' to credit the song variously to Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer. The song was a commercial and critical success and was nominated for Vocal Event of the Year at the 2003 [[Country Music Association]] awards.

"Picture" is a duet written by American music artists Kid Rock and Sheryl Crow, released on November 12, 2002, as the fourth single and ninth track from Kid Rock's 2001 album Cocky. The original recording on the album is performed by the song's writers. Rock re-recorded the song for radio with alternative country singer Allison Moorer because Atlantic was initially unable to get the rights from Crow's label to release the album version as a single. When the Moorer version was released, some radio stations began playing the Crow version instead, leading Billboard to credit the song variously to Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer. The song was a commercial and critical success and was nominated for Vocal Event of the Year at the 2003 Country Music Association awards.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Kid Rock's label, [[Atlantic Records]], was unable to obtain permission from Crow's label, [[A&M Records]], to release the original version as a single.  Therefore, Atlantic Records decided to rework the song with country singer [[Allison Moorer]] (coincidentally signed to A&M's sister label [[Show Dog-Universal Music|Universal South Records]]) instead. Moorer re-recorded Crow’s vocals for the radio release.<ref name=Kaufman>{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Gil|title=Kid Rock's Dead-In-The-Water Cocky Comes Back To Life|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1459755/20030129/kid_rock.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030201094103/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1459755/20030129/kid_rock.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 1, 2003|work=MTV News|access-date=September 9, 2017|date=January 29, 2003}}</ref>

Even though Atlantic Records was unable to obtain rights to release Crow's version as a single, mainstream, rock/alternative, and some country radio stations disregarded this and played the original version featuring Crow, while other country music radio stations played the radio edit featuring Allison Moorer instead. Because of this, ''Billboard'' credited the song on the charts as Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Masley|first1=Ed|title=15 Best Kid Rock Singles, from 'Bawitdaba' to 'First Kiss'|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/entertainment/music/2015/08/21/best-kid-rock-singles-bawitdaba-first-kiss/32117495/|access-date=September 9, 2017|work=Arizona Republic|via=azcentral.com|date=August 21, 2015}}</ref> Each version of the song features a different guitar solo.

Therefore, Atlantic Records decided to rework the song with country singer Allison Moorer (coincidentally signed to A&M's sister label Universal South Records) instead. Even though Atlantic Records was unable to obtain rights to release Crow's version as a single, mainstream, rock/alternative, and some country radio stations disregarded this and played the original version featuring Crow, while other country music radio stations played the radio edit featuring Allison Moorer instead. Because of this, Billboard credited the song on the charts as Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer. Each version of the song features a different guitar solo.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is performed in the key of [[G major]] in [[Time signature|common time]] with a [[tempo]] of 98 beats per minute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spotontrack.com/track/picture-feat-sheryl-crow/1098344|title=Picture (feat. Sheryl Crow) - Sheryl Crow, Kid Rock - Spot On Track|website=www.spotontrack.com|access-date=August 27, 2017}}</ref>  The verses of the song follow a chord progression of G–C–D–C–G, and the chorus follows an Em–G–D–C–G progression. The vocals span from G<sub>2</sub> to D<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0043998|title=Kid Rock "Picture" Sheet Music in G Major (transposable) - Download & Print|last=Rock|first=Kid|website=Musicnotes.com|date=March 31, 2003 |access-date=August 27, 2017}}</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
Being the third Kid Rock single that entered ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'''s [[Hot 100]] chart, "Picture" remains his highest-charting single in the United States, peaking at {{abbr|No.|Number}} 4 in April 2003. The song also charted on the [[Hot Country Singles & Tracks]] chart, peaking at No. 21. Until 2008's "[[All Summer Long (Kid Rock song)|All Summer Long]]", it also marked his only top-40 country hit. The song is also Sheryl Crow's second-most successful single in the United States, after her 1994 hit "[[All I Wanna Do (Sheryl Crow song)|All I Wanna Do]]" which reached No. 2. It is Kid Rock's only top-10 hit on the Hot 100.

On the Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, the song was credited only to Kid Rock and Crow for 22 weeks. By then, the single had reached No. 33 on the chart.<ref>[http://www.billboard.com/charts/2003-03-08/country-songs]{{dead link|date=July 2011}}</ref> The following week, however, the song began to be credited to Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer.<ref>[http://www.billboard.com/charts/2003-03-15/country-songs]{{dead link|date=July 2011}}</ref> The song spent a total of 33 weeks on the country chart, reaching No. 21 in 2003.<ref>[http://www.billboard.com/charts/2003-05-24/country-songs]{{dead link|date=July 2011}}</ref> As of September 2017, "Picture" sold 836,300 copies in the United States according to [[Nielsen SoundScan]].<ref name="ussales">{{cite news|url=http://www.defjampromo.com/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-9-14-17.pdf|title=Nielsen SoundScan charts – Digital Songs – Week Ending: 09/14/2017|publisher=[[Nielsen SoundScan]]|access-date=September 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170919211714/http://www.defjampromo.com/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-9-14-17.pdf|archive-date=September 19, 2017}}</ref>
sections.text:
Being the third Kid Rock single that entered Billboards Hot 100 chart, "Picture" remains his highest-charting single in the United States, peaking at {{abbr|No.|Number}} 4 in April 2003. The song also charted on the Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, peaking at No. 21. Until 2008's "All Summer Long", it also marked his only top-40 country hit. The song is also Sheryl Crow's second-most successful single in the United States, after her 1994 hit "All I Wanna Do" which reached No. 2. It is Kid Rock's only top-10 hit on the Hot 100.

On the Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, the song was credited only to Kid Rock and Crow for 22 weeks. By then, the single had reached No. 33 on the chart. The following week, however, the song began to be credited to Kid Rock featuring Sheryl Crow or Allison Moorer. The song spent a total of 33 weeks on the country chart, reaching No. 21 in 2003. As of September 2017, "Picture" sold 836,300 copies in the United States according to Nielsen SoundScan.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: Even though Crow's label did not release licensing permissions for the original version, Crow was featured in the music video singing instead of Moorer.  The video takes place in a studio showing Rock and Crow recording the song, accompanied by clips of the duo hanging out in the winter time. During the guitar solo, Rock is seen wearing a cowboy hat and winter jacket while walking alone in a field covered in snow. The video also features a few uses of the [[monochrome]] effect, while most of the video is in [[color]]. It was directed by JB Carlin.

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext: Kid Rock performed "Picture" with [[LeAnn Rimes]] on his 2003 Christmas TV special, ''A Kid Rock Christmas''. A live performance he had of the song with [[Gretchen Wilson]] was released as a track on his 2006 album ''[[Live Trucker]]''. He performed the song at a concert with [[Martina McBride]] for the 2009 TV special ''[[CMA Music Festival]]: Country's Night to Rock''.<ref>{{cite web |title=ABC rocks country fans with CMA Music Festival: Country's Night To Rock |url=https://www.channelguidemag.com/tv-news/2009/08/13/abc-rocks-country-fans-with-cma-music-festival-countrys-night-to-rock/ |date=August 13, 2009 |first=Lori |last=Acken |publisher=Channel Guide Magazine}}</ref> Kid Rock has also sung the song live with female country singers [[Kellie Pickler]], [[Miranda Lambert]] and [[Jessie James]]. When the song is performed live, the music pauses while Kid Rock holds out the lyric "I was off to drink you away", following the lyric "I was headed to church".
sections.text: Kid Rock performed "Picture" with LeAnn Rimes on his 2003 Christmas TV special, A Kid Rock Christmas. A live performance he had of the song with Gretchen Wilson was released as a track on his 2006 album Live Trucker. He performed the song at a concert with Martina McBride for the 2009 TV special CMA Music Festival: Country's Night to Rock. Kid Rock has also sung the song live with female country singers Kellie Pickler, Miranda Lambert and Jessie James. When the song is performed live, the music pauses while Kid Rock holds out the lyric "I was off to drink you away", following the lyric "I was headed to church".
